implementation.mechanism: Singleton transactional bigint revision updated by an AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE OR TRUNCATE statement trigger catches every committed statement, even unchanged updated_at and direct SQL from another connection. Every cache call reads that one revision; cold rows and stamp share REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY snapshot. A concurrent commit is visible on the next call, rollback changes neither visible stamp nor rows. Query errors propagate; no TTL/stale-on-error answer. Fresh get/get_by_persona/list_by_tenant/list_all remain uncached.
implementation.cache: Store-local full row inputs, detached deep copies, LRU 8 keys / 32 MiB per key / 64 MiB retained recursive object budget; no cross-service helper was suitable because Registry cache relies on its own stored summary_rev/index/delta model.

implementation.first_deploy_startup: PostgresPersonaProvisioningStore.__init__ synchronously calls _bootstrap before returning the store. On the first BFF start against the old populated ledger, CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS creates the revision table, INSERT establishes its singleton, and CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION/TRIGGER installs transactional invalidation before the first directory read. All bootstrap statements commit together on context exit; failure prevents store construction rather than answering with an unvalidated cache. No separate prior migration run is required. test_postgres_first_start_upgrades_existing_ledger_before_directory_reads removes the revision table/function/trigger from a real 170-row local Postgres ledger, reconstructs the store, compares cold/warm snapshot and both HTTP payloads with the full baseline (HTTP 200), and verifies the first post-upgrade write invalidates the warmed cache. Hosted role/schema ownership and CREATE privilege are task-author read-only facts, not worker verification.
